name: files__read_multiple_files
description: Read the contents of multiple files in one call. Provide a list of file paths to read, and optionally specify an encoding, whether to include file metadata, whether to ignore read errors, and a separator string between file contents.

ignoreErrors.description: Silently skip files that cannot be read instead of including error messages

includeMetadata.description: Prepend file metadata (size, last modified) before each file's content

paths.description: Array of file paths to read

separator.description: Separator string inserted between file contents (default: '---')

name: tasks__tasks_add
description: Add new tasks with a specific status. It's faster and cheaper if you use this in batch. User can add atomically while AI works using the CLI add tool

index.description:
0-based index to place the tasks. e.g.:
- 0 for "Do this next"
- Omit to place at the end ("Do this later")

source_id.description:
Source ID from task_setup() response
- Defaults to most recent in the workspace if not provided
- Try to always provide it!
- If you don't have it, ask the user for a file path and call task_setup()

status.description:
You might need to infer it from the context:
- "To Do" for tasks coming up next (e.g. "Do X next")
- "In Progress" for what you'll do now (e.g. "First do X")
- "Reminders" instructions for you (the AI) to be constantly reminded of
- "Notes" to collect non-actionable notes

name: tasks__tasks_setup
description:
Initializes a source file from a path.
- Always call this once per conversation when asked to use these tools
- If the file path is not provided, ask the user to clarify it before calling this tool
- Creates the file if it does not already exist
- Returns the source ID for subsequent use
- Use mcp-tasks tools when the user mentions new or updated tasks

workspace.description: Workspace or project directory path, typically provided by the IDE or set to $PWD
